title: Reproducible model build + cryptographic tagging and canary publishing pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
We need a CI/CD flow that consistently produces reproducible model artifacts, binds verifiable provenance to each artifact, signs artifacts using our customer/HSM-backed keyring, and publishes performance profiles to the catalog with staged channel promotion (staging -> canary -> stable). Current onboarding steps are manual and error-prone: model builders push artifacts, maintainers manually generate perf profiles, and release engineers do ad-hoc pinning. This adds latency to model publishing and increases risk of unsigned or unproven artifacts making it into Dedicated/Private environments.

Goals:
- Produce bit-reproducible model artifacts from deterministic build environment (pinned base images / build containers).
- Generate a standard provenance bundle (SBOM + build recipe + deterministic hashes) compatible with an in-toto-like verifier.
- Sign artifacts and provenance using KMS/HSM-backed keys; record signature metadata for audit.
- Run automated perf profile jobs (latency P50/P95, token cost, throughput) using a shaded benchmark harness and store structured profile JSONs in the model catalog.
- Implement staged channel promotion: staging -> canary (small traffic) -> stable with automated gating and rollback on regressions.
- Auto-pin model versions in the catalog when promoted to stable and provide explicit unpin flow.

Proposed design (high level):
1) CI build job (model-cd/build): reproducible builder executes the model conversion (hf -> optimized artifact), normalizes metadata and outputs: model.tar, sbom.json, build.recipe.txt. The build job records deterministic inputs (git commit, base image digest, conversion tool version).
2) Provenance bundler (model-cd/provenance): collates sbom+recipe+hashes into prov.bundle.json, signs bundle with KMS key (use edge HSM via KMS_SIGN role), and uploads artifacts to artifact-bucket with immutability tags.
3) Perf job (model-cd/perf): spins sandboxed runner (dedicated small GPU), runs representative prompt set and traces P50/P95/throughput and token cost; outputs profile-{commit}.json and regression metrics.
4) Publish step: atomically register artifact + provenance + performance profile to the model catalog under a staging channel with metadata: {version, commit, signatures, profile_id}.
5) Canary controller (model-cd/canary): after staging registration, automated canary promotion job deploys model variant to a small traffic slice (internal tests + 1% customer mimic), monitors SLOs for 24h, evaluates against gating rules (latency p95 delta < 10%, cost delta < 15%, error rate < 0.1%), and either promotes to stable (auto-pin) or triggers rollback and notifies owners.
6) Pinning and catalog APIs: when stable promotion completes, the model catalog API auto-updates pinned_version (with audit entry) and emits console events for Redwood Console to show pinned change. Unpin requires explicit approval (UI + CLI).

Security and audit considerations:
- All signing uses KMS keys with restricted IAM; rotate keys per policy and record key id in provenance bundle.
- Provenance stored in attestations store and mirrored to S3 with retention policy.
- Build environment must execute in ephemeral runners with network egress controls; no secrets left in artifacts.

Acceptance criteria:
- CI job produces reproducible artifact for the same input commit (identical digest) in >= 3 repeat builds in separate runners.
- Every published artifact has a signed provenance bundle in the catalog and the signature verifies using our KMS public key.
- Automatic perf job runs on every staging publish and stores profile JSON accessible by console and API.
- Canary promotions run automatically and follow gating rules; stable promotion auto-pins the version and writes audit event.
- Rollback path tested end-to-end (simulate perf regression -> automatic rollback observed).

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (PoC): implement build + provenance sign + storage for internal models (2 sprints).
- Phase 2 (Perf): add perf harness and publish pipeline; integrate with catalog in staging (1 sprint).
- Phase 3 (Canary): implement canary controller with gating and auto-pin (2 sprints).
- Phase 4: Enable for public onboarding, documentation, and on-prem operator docs (1 sprint).

Operational notes:
- Provide dashboards for publish events, canary health, and audit trail in Console.
- Create runbook for signature verification and rollback triggers.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Use in-toto vs custom simple provenance format (we selected a small subset of in-toto fields for MVP).
- How strict should the reproducibility requirement be for non-deterministic conversion tools (quantize steps)? Proposal: require deterministic mode where available, otherwise tag as non-reproducible and restrict to staging-only until manual review.

Links / artifacts:
- Design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/Model+CD+Provenance+Design
- Benchmark harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-bench
- PoC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-cd/pull/275

Next steps:
- Kick off 1-week PoC to validate signing flow and reproducible build on our ephemeral runners.
- Schedule security sync with infra (KMS/HSM) and compliance.
- Draft initial gating rules and thresholds with SRE and product owners.
